notes.text: - **Kalyanakaraka = Ugradityacharya** (G2 2012, 2019; APPSC PYQ ×3); Somadeva Suri, Padmaprabha Maladhari Deva and Revana Siddha are distractors.

q: Who received the title of 'Gandharva Vidya Visarada' in the Chalukya court?
explanation: Chellavva (Challavva), court dancer and singer of Chalukya Bhima I, received the title Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada and the village Attili; Mallappa was her father, Chamekamba a courtesan of Ammaraja II's time, Bhattadeva a court poet.

notes.text: - **Who:** **Chellavva (Challavva / Chellava)** – court **singer and dancer** of **Chalukya Bhima I** (G2 2011 ×2; APPSC PYQ).
- **Titles:** **Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada** (G2 Mains 2019 ×2; APPSC PYQ ×2) and **Samasta Gandharva Vidya Kovida**.

q: Which Agama is common for Ramanuja and Madhva Philosophers?
explanation: Both Ramanuja (Sri Vaishnavism) and Madhva follow the Pancharatra Agama; Vaikhanasa is the other Vaishnava agama, used at Tirumala, and Shaakta/Jangama are non-Vaishnava.

notes.text: - **⚠ Trap:** Pancharatra and Vaikhanasa are **Vaishnava**, not Shaiva or Shakta.

q: The early Chalukyas worshipped this mother goddess?
explanation: The Chalukyas called themselves Hariti-putras (sons of Hariti) of the Manavya gotra, nourished by the Seven Mothers; Rocket lists Hariti as the mother goddess worshipped by the early Chalukyas. Kushmandini is a Jain yakshi, not the Chalukya family goddess (printed key: Cushmandini).

notes.text: - **Mother goddess of the early Chalukyas:** **Hariti** – the Chalukyas called themselves **Hariti-putras** of the **Manavya gotra**, nourished by the **Seven Mothers** (Saptamatrikas) (G2 2019).
- **Same goddess, other dynasty:** Hariti was also the tutelary deity of the **Ikshvakus**; the metronymic "Hariti-putra" suggests a southern origin of the Eastern Chalukyas.

q: Nayanmar's belongs to the convention of
explanation: The Nayanars (63 Tamil saints) were devotees of Shiva, i.e. the Saiva tradition; the Alvars were the Vaishnava saints.

q: Gramadevata temples belong to which tradition?
explanation: Gramadevata (village goddess) shrines belong to the Shakta (Sakteya) tradition of mother-goddess worship.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
q: Which religious sect enjoyed great popularity under eastern Chalukyas of Vengi?
explanation: Saivism dominated under the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi: kings built Shiva temples (Biccavolu, Draksharama), and Buddharamas became Saiva shrines. Jainism and Buddhism declined.

notes.text: - **Shaivism dominant:** sects **Pasupata** (founder **Lakulisha**, oldest, peaceful), **Kalamukha** (extremist) and **Kapalika** (Bhairava worship).
- **Declining:** Buddharamas became Shaiva temples (Dhanyakataka → Amareswara); Hiuen Tsang (639) found Buddhist sites decaying; survived at **Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda**.

q: What did the word 'Udranga' refer to during the ancient Chalukya period?
explanation:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Fixed (principal) land tax); it is added as option 5.
No option is right: D.C. Sircar's Indian Epigraphical Glossary explains udranga as the fixed or principal land tax (tax on permanent tenants), paired with uparikara (minor taxes); it is not a toll, salt, water or shop tax. The older app key 'tax on water' has no source support.

notes.text: - **Udranga:** in epigraphy the **fixed or principal land tax** (tax on permanent tenants), paired with **uparikara** (minor taxes) – D.C. Sircar.
- **⚠ Settled:** "Udranga = tax on water" (old app key) has no source support; a PYQ offering only tolls / salt / water / shop tax has no correct option.

q: Which was the central location of trade guilds in medieval Andhra?
explanation: Penugonda (West Godavari) was the headquarters of the merchant guilds of medieval Andhra and seat of goddess Vasavi; Bejwada was a trade centre but not the guild headquarters.

notes.text: - **Penugonda (West Godavari)** = **headquarters of the merchant guilds** of medieval Andhra and main seat of goddess **Vasavi** (APPSC PYQ).

q: In which of the following Indian states is the Nedumbi Basadi rock-cut Jain cave temple located?
explanation: Nedumbi Basadi was a Jain basadi built at Bezawada (Vijayawada) by Ayyana Mahadevi, queen of the Eastern Chalukya Kubja Vishnuvardhana, so it is in Andhra Pradesh.

q: Among the Vengi Chalukya rulers in Andhra, who built many temples?
explanation: Chalukya Bhima I, who fought 360 battles, is said to have built 360 temples, including the Pancharamas and the Bhimeswara temples of Draksharama and Samalkot.

notes.text: - **Chalukya Bhima I** (892-922): fought **360 battles** (Pithapuram inscription of Mallapadeva) and is said to have built **360 temples**; "the Vengi ruler who built many temples" (APPSC PYQ).
- **Pancharamas built by:** **Chalukya Bhima I**, i.e. under the **Vengi (Eastern) Chalukyas** (APPSC PYQ ×2) – not Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Pulakesin II, Rajaraja Narendra, Kakatiyas or Vijayanagara.

q: Founder of famous Draksharama temple?
explanation: Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeswara temple at Draksharama; Gunaga Vijayaditya built the Bikkavolu group and Vijayaditya II the 108 Narendreswara temples.

notes.text: - **Draksharama founder:** **Chalukya Bhima I** built the **Bhimeswara** temple (G2 1993); an **Eastern Chalukya** monument, not Pallava or Satavahana.
- **Chalukya Bhima I** (892-922): fought **360 battles** (Pithapuram inscription of Mallapadeva) and is said to have built **360 temples**; "the Vengi ruler who built many temples" (APPSC PYQ).

q: In which place Chalukya Bhimavaram founded by Chalukya Bhima is situated in Andhra?
explanation: Chalukya Bhimavaram is Samalkot (Samarlakota), seat of Kumararama, built by Chalukya Bhima I in memory of his son; Pithapuram and Draksharama are separate towns and Gunupudi is Somarama.

notes.text: - **Chalukya Bhimavaram = Samalkot (Samarlakota)** (Welfare Officers 2017) – not Pithapuram, Draksharama or Gudipudi.
